payload.unusable_reason: Not a motor accident compensation claim: a vehicle buyer's own-damage insurance claim for theft of the vehicle, decided by the consumer fora (District Forum, State Commission, NCDRC) and then the Supreme Court. No death or injury and no Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal award.

extraction.title_anon: Vehicle theft insurance claim by a vehicle buyer, Punjab (not a motor accident claim)
extraction.family_summary: A firm bought a repossessed vehicle at a bank auction in 2006 and insured it, but the vehicle was stolen weeks later and the insurer refused to pay because the registration was still in the old owner's name. The consumer forums turned the claim down. In July 2019, about 13 years after the theft, the Supreme Court ordered the insurer to pay the auction price with interest. This is an insurance dispute over a stolen vehicle, not compensation for a road crash.
what_mattered: The insurer had taken the premium from the buyer and had been told by the bank of the transfer, so it could not refuse the claim just because the registration certificate was not yet transferred.
The Court kept own-damage insurance separate from third-party liability: the rule that the registered owner stays liable to accident victims was left untouched.
